subject: MSA & Order Form — notice windows and exit terms
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@fintegrate.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@fintegrate.com
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: term & exit language

Vanessa —

Thanks for sending the latest MSA and order form. We've run this past our legal and procurement teams and have two outstanding asks on term/renewal/termination that we need clarified before I can route for final approval:

1) Auto-renewal: We prefer an opt-in renewal (no automatic renewal) or at minimum a 60-day written notice window prior to renewal. Your current language auto-renews for an additional 12 months unless notice is provided 30 days prior.

2) Termination for convenience: We need a 60-day termination-for-convenience right on the Order Form rather than the 90-day period in the current draft; if Redwood requires a 90-day window, we’d ask for a pro-rated credit for unused committed capacity.

I've attached our marked-up redlines (Fintegrate_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx) and the populated order form. Please confirm whether Redwood's legal can accept these or provide counter language we can present to our procurement committee.

Best,
Maya Singh
Director, Strategic Procurement
Fintegrate Inc.


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@fintegrate.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: term & exit language

Maya —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I've looped in Lauren (legal ops) and Karthik (AE) so we can coordinate internally. High-level response:

- Auto-renewal: We can discuss extending the notice window to 60 days in the MSA but want to preserve an auto-renew mechanism for operational continuity. If procurement is firm on opt-in, we can escalate to legal, but it may change pricing cadence.
- Termination for convenience: 60 days is not unusual; our standard is 90 days without a pro-rata credit. We may be able to offer a pro-rated credit or a phased wind-down commitment, subject to deal size.

I'll get Rachel to review the attached markups and propose counters that balance your needs and our service continuity. Karthik — can you confirm whether Fintegrate is planning a single-year order or multi-year commit? That affects what concessions we can make.

Next steps: internal review today, will aim to get a proposed MSA patch back to you by Monday.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines: term & exit language

Team —

I've reviewed the Fintegrate redlines. Notes below:

1) Auto-renewal / Notice window
- Proposal A (counter): Keep auto-renew but extend notice window to 60 days for annual renewals. Add a Customer Notification clause requiring Redwood to send renewal notice no later than 75 days prior to the renewal effective date (gives both sides margin).
- Proposal B (if customer insists on opt-in): Allow opt-in only for deals <= 12 months and under $50k ARR; for larger/longer commitments we require auto-renew to avoid operational churn.

2) Termination for Convenience
- We can accept 60-day termination for convenience on the Order Form, with mutually agreed wind-down terms. If customer terminates early on a committed multi-year Order Form, propose a termination fee equal to the lesser of 3 months' committed fees or the remaining term's committed fees (standard commercial compromise).

3) Pro-rated credits
- We typically do not offer pro-rata credits for committed capacity cancellations; instead we offer either transition credits or service credits applied to future invoices. If the customer needs cash refunds, we will require an approval from Finance and a shorter termination window will likely come with a higher termination fee.

I'll draft specific redline language for both clauses and include an option set so the customer can pick. Vanessa — want me to send as tracked changes in the doc or as clean clause options in the email?

R
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: term & exit language

Maya —

Quick note from deal-side: Fintegrate is targeting a 3-year deployment across two product tiers (pilot year + scale years). We are not expecting this to be a small single-year order. That said, open to working with you on fair exit terms — our priority is to avoid operational risk where we allocate reserved capacity.

If it helps the committee, Redwood can accept a 60-day termination-for-convenience on the Order Form for the pilot year only, with a 90-day standard thereafter, or we can keep 90 days and build in a phased prorate/credit for unused committed capacity if we go multi-year.

Happy to jump on a short call to resolve.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive
